root_cause.text: The DualShock4 HID parser (`dualshock4_parse_report` in `hid-playstation.c`) trusted the device-controlled `num_touch_reports` field and used it as the loop bound without clamping it to the fixed `touch_reports[]` array size, allowing out-of-bounds reads when a device reports too many touch entries.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `num_touch_reports = usb->num_touch_reports;` and `num_touch_reports = bt->num_touch_reports;` to `min_t(u8, ... , ARRAY_SIZE(...->touch_reports))`, and the CVE states that otherwise the loop “will read off the end of the touch_reports array” for up to 256 iterations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the DualShock 4 touch report count to the backing array size to avoid out-of-bounds processing.
intent_record.what: In dualshock4_parse_report(), the assignment to num_touch_reports was changed from using usb->num_touch_reports directly to using min_t(u8, usb->num_touch_reports, ARRAY_SIZE(usb->touch_reports)).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the parser now caps the number of touch reports it will process to the actual size of the usb->touch_reports array, preventing iteration beyond the allocated storage if usb->num_touch_reports is larger than the array capacity.

Author: Roderick Colenbrander <roderick@gaikai.com>

    HID: playstation: add DualShock4 touchpad support.
    
    Support the DualShock4 touchpad as a separate input device. The code
    describes the touchpad input reports through structures similar a bit
    to the DualSense code.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this diff. The code trusts the device-controlled field directly: `num_touch_reports = usb->num_touch_reports;` and then uses it as the loop bound: `for (i = 0; i < num_touch_reports; i++) { struct dualshock4_touch_report *touch_report = &touch_reports[i]; ... }`. There is no clamping or validation against the fixed-size array `touch_reports[3]`, so a malicious device could report too many touch entries and drive `touch_reports[i]` out of bounds. The fix is not present because there is no check limiting `num_touch_reports` to the array size before indexing.
